qs.q: A clinical audit evaluates invasive diagnostic tests for prenatal genetics. Which procedure carries the highest associated procedure-related miscarriage risk among the standard options?
qs.e: Cordocentesis carries a miscarriage risk of 1-2%, which is higher than amniocentesis (0.1-0.5%) and CVS (0.5-1%). Screening tests carry no procedural miscarriage risk as they are non-invasive.
qs.s: Prenatal Genetic Counselling and Screening: Down Syndrome, NIPT, CVS: MCQs

qs.q: A clinical audit evaluates risk factors for male breast cancer. Which of the following conditions is specifically noted to increase the relative risk of developing breast cancer in men?
qs.e: Klinefelter syndrome is a well-established risk factor that mirrors the hormonal imbalances and increased relative risks seen in female breast carcinogenesis. Benign prostatic hyperplasia does not share this established causal association.
qs.s: Breast Cancer Guide: Epidemiology, Risk Factors & Classification: MCQs

qs.q: A clinical audit reviews why primary care physicians struggled to utilize the 1990 ACR classification criteria for widespread pain syndromes. What was a major practical limitation of these criteria?
o: It failed to include widespread pain as a core symptom
It was too complex to perform without specialist software
Physicians often did not know how to examine tender points
It required expensive laboratory testing and imaging
qs.e: A major limitation was physicians not knowing how to examine tender points correctly or omitting the physical exam entirely. Laboratory tests and imaging are not part of these traditional criteria.
